findings.title: Security group ingress open to the world
findings.description: Ingress rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 expose the workload to the entire internet. Restrict source CIDRs to known ranges.
findings.remediation:
Restrict the ingress CIDR to trusted ranges. Replace `0.0.0.0/0` with your
office/VPN CIDRs, or remove the rule and use SSM Session Manager (no inbound
SSH needed):
ingress {
  from_port   = 22
  to_port     = 22
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]  # your trusted range
}

findings.title: Security group or rule without description
findings.description: Hygiene: Security groups and their rules should carry descriptions so reviewers understand their purpose. Add a description attribute.
findings.expected: description attribute documenting the group or rule
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GCS bucket publicly readable via IAM
findings.description: A bucket IAM binding/member granting objectViewer or admin to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers exposes bucket data to the internet.
findings.remediation:
Remove `allUsers` / `allAuthenticatedUsers` from the bucket IAM policy. Grant
`roles/storage.objectViewer` only to specific service accounts or groups:
resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "viewer" {
  bucket = google_storage_bucket.this.name
  role   = "roles/storage.objectViewer"
  member = "serviceAccount:app@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}

findings.title: GCS bucket without uniform bucket-level access
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with uniform_bucket_level_access = false allows per-object ACLs, which can silently expose individual objects. Enable uniform access to manage permissions via IAM only.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GCS bucket without versioning
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with versioning disabled or absent loses protection against accidental overwrites and deletions.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: GCS bucket without customer-managed encryption
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with no encryption block uses Google-managed keys. Customer-managed (CMEK) keys are required for regulated data.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. Google-managed keys apply by default; for regulated data use customer-managed keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS with key rotation.

findings.title: GCS bucket without access logging
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with no logging block has no audit trail of object access.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity + Data Access), VPC flow logs, and Security Command Center. Ship logs to a dedicated project with locked retention.

findings.title: GCS bucket without lifecycle rules
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with no lifecycle_rule accumulates objects indefinitely; hygiene finding.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: GCS bucket without public access prevention
findings.description: google_storage_bucket without public_access_prevention = "enforced" can be made public via ACLs or IAM.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public IPs / public access, and use Private Service Connect / VPC Service Controls if external access is required. Verify with `gcloud compute firewall-rules list`.

findings.title: GCS bucket without soft-delete protection
findings.description: google_storage_bucket with no soft_delete_policy block loses the safety net that retains deleted objects for recovery. Configure soft_delete_policy to guard against accidental or malicious deletion.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
